about: Reviewed Simpson-Resnick cross-witness set (developer's evidence-level review, 2026-11-03). Four groups: established conflicts (expected "conflict"; none in this set), review-worthy disagreements needing context ("conflict_needs_context"; never strict positives), verified negative controls ("no_conflict"), and exploratory cases ("exploratory"; never scored). Candidates were drafted from the transcripts by a Claude agent and every one was decided by the developer. Archive-derived exports, not certified transcripts; lines are the archive's statement numbers, with the part for the Jan 23, 1996 file.

pairs.topic: June 5, 1994 dog incident at Bundy: how Kato got out (front gate vs garage)
pairs.note: Reviewer: review-worthy, not established. Front gate (Simpson) vs garage door (Resnick) for the same June 5 visit; not established that two distinct openings are impossible. Anchors widened to the location statements.

pairs.topic: June 5, 1994: whether Simpson went down Nicole's side alleyway
pairs.note: Reviewer: review-worthy. They disagree on whether Simpson entered the side alleyway; visibility and observation limits matter.

pairs.topic: nervous breakdown and Puerto Rico calls
pairs.note: Reviewer: retained provisionally as a review-worthy disagreement. Simpson says Nicole reported a nervous breakdown and that he discussed it with Faye, who blamed Cora. Resnick denies knowledge of a nervous breakdown and denies that Simpson discussed that subject with her. Both accounts support that calls occurred; do not label as proven contradiction. (source label: conflicting_accounts / candidate_conflict_with_context)

pairs.topic: Funeral: 'I loved her too much' remark to Faye Resnick
pairs.note: Reviewer: no-recollection control. Simpson's answer begins "I don't recall".

pairs.topic: May 1994 breakup: who ended the relationship
pairs.note: Reviewer: control. The conversations may have occurred on different dates (Resnick about May 2-3; Simpson May 7-9).

pairs.topic: June 12, 1994 recital: whether Nicole told Simpson to leave her alone
pairs.note: Reviewer: control. The accounts may describe different times or settings (Resnick relays Nicole; Simpson speaks to the recital and the 8:45 call).

pairs.topic: Nicole 'in trouble' in January 1994
pairs.note: Reviewer: knowledge-difference control. Resnick speaks to her general impression and could not know of the call.

pairs.topic: When Resnick entered treatment after the intervention
pairs.note: Reviewer: negative control (secondhand_consistent).

pairs.topic: Who called the intervention
pairs.note: Reviewer: negative control (secondhand_consistent).

pairs.topic: Resnick's condition on June 5, 1994
pairs.note: Reviewer: negative control (compatible).

pairs.topic: Last encounter between Simpson and Resnick before the murder
pairs.note: Reviewer: negative control (compatible).

pairs.topic: Socializing as couples (Simpson/Nicole with Resnick/Reichardt)
pairs.note: Reviewer: negative control (compatible).

pairs.topic: Simpson caring for Nicole during her pneumonia (mid-May 1994)
pairs.note: Reviewer: negative control (secondhand_consistent).

pairs.topic: October 1993 Gretna Green door incident
pairs.note: Reviewer: negative control (secondhand_consistent).

pairs.topic: telephone calls while Simpson in Puerto Rico
pairs.note: Reviewer: retained as a negative control. Both accounts support that Simpson was in Puerto Rico and calls with Faye occurred. The content of the calls is tested separately by CW-001. (source label: compatible_context / no_conflict)

pairs.topic: different time periods for drug use
pairs.note: Reviewer: retained as a negative control. Simpson's answers concern January-June 1994; Resnick's observations concern October and December 1993. Do not infer a conflict across non-overlapping periods. (source label: non_overlapping_time_scope / no_conflict)

pairs.topic: Toscana dinner, March 1994: Resnick's pills
pairs.note: Reviewer: exploratory, unscored. Resnick does not clearly deny that pills were taken from her.

pairs.topic: Return of the bracelet and earrings (May 1994): why Nicole gave them back
pairs.note: Reviewer: exploratory, unscored. The different explanations for returning the jewelry are not necessarily mutually exclusive.

pairs.topic: Resnick at Nicole's house in May 1994: different weeks
pairs.note: Reviewer: exploratory, excluded from scored controls: imprecise dates, and presence is not the same as observation.

pairs.topic: cocaine use in 1993
pairs.note: Reviewer: exploratory discovery target, not an established contradiction until the complete denial and counsel's interruption are reviewed; unscored. Resnick gives affirmative firsthand observations in October and December 1993. Simpson's relevant answer was interrupted by counsel and he refused the follow-up question; this is not a clean denial and must not be scored as an unqualified contradiction. (source label: potential_conflict_procedural_qualification / needs_context_not_clean_positive)

exclusions.reason: Dropped by the reviewer: double hearsay (Reichardt via Simpson), no time frame, likely consistent with Resnick's admitted relapse.
Dropped by the reviewer: not clear that the Playboy work is the business venture Resnick means.
